results.reason: Issue 5 cites § 2.2 automatic five-year renewals and the 270/240-day notice band. It calls this a narrow 30-day window and explains that missing it locks Harrowgate in for another five years.

Issue 1 quotes § 3.1 (all glass and PET containers, any beverage product, worldwide) and contrasts it with the term sheet's amber glass/beer/US-Canada scope. Issue 8 explains the integration clause locks in the broader executed text.

Issue 3 cites Recital C (14% increase, receipt August 3, 2026). It states the 30-day window expired September 2, 2026, before the September 21 amendment, so the increase is deemed accepted under § 5.4.

Issue 2 explains that Amendment § 2.1 replaces § 11.2, deletes the recall-cost exclusion, and limits the indemnity carve-out to § 9.1(c) IP claims. It states recall, defect and personal-injury exposure is now subject to the six-month-fees cap.

Issue 6 identifies new § 14.4 permitting assignment without consent to Affiliates and successors. However, it never states that nothing prevents assignment to a competitor, and never notes that Harrowgate remains bound by consent, making the restriction one-sided.
The response never cites Section 15.2 or the order-of-precedence rule under which the amendment controls over the Supply Agreement.
The response refers to the § 11.1 cap as 'six months of container fees' and the 'six-month-fees cap', conveying that the cap equals six months of fees.
It is a memo addressed to [Partner], with numbered issues. Each issue has a 'Where' section citation and a 'Recommended fix'.
It provides proposed contract language, including a narrowed § 3.1, a restored § 11.2, and a revised § 14.4.
It concludes the objection window closed and the increase is deemed accepted. It suggests only exploring a challenge based on a possibly deficient notice, not a timely objection.
It does not treat the term sheet as binding. It states the integration clause supersedes the term sheet and the deviations are locked in as written.
